adopted: warp: NEON float64x2 pairs (clang + aarch64 + NEON, not FPM_DISABLE_SIMD) mirroring the fused scalar expressions; pairs with any pixel outside 0<=sx<w-1, 0<=sy<h-1 and the odd tail use the unchanged scalar warpPixel
pyrDown: direct taps for interior columns, reflect101 only at the edges, reflected row pointers once per output row; integer arithmetic unchanged

rejected_in_pilot.variant: A: scalar loop with an interior fast path
rejected_in_pilot.reason: about 8-20% faster warp only; dropped so the scalar reference loop stays literal

rejected_in_pilot.variant: B: NEON pairs with per-pixel double gathers through the stack
D: C unrolled to four pixels
rejected_in_pilot.reason: about 3-12% faster warp than C in the pilot, not worth a second unrolled copy

failures_and_caveats: the NEON path reproduces clang's default -ffp-contract=on fusion; other compilers (GCC) keep the scalar loop and a different contraction flag would be caught by rotation/pyramid/exact-reference
the uint8 output is not proof of identical intermediates in general, but mutant W2 (one multiply-add left unfused) was caught by the exact-reference test
rotation SIMD is compile-time only: Backend::Scalar still selects only the scalar dot product, so portable_scalar mode also got faster (-9.9%)
pilot micro outputs were rerun once after selection to archive them; the selection used the earlier, unarchived runs with the same ordering
